units.passage: Do not upload a recording of a lecture, discussion, or any other person to an AI tool without the instructor's permission.
units.why: 'Do not upload a recording of a lecture, discussion, or any other person to an AI tool without the instructor's permission': P49.

units.passage: Additionally, you should never use course materials or assignments as a prompt for an AI tool, unless explicitly allowed by the course policy.
units.why: Students 'should never use course materials or assignments as a prompt for an AI tool, unless explicitly allowed by the course policy'. Keeping course materials and assignments out of AI tools is P49, which names both; P20 would cover the assignment but not the course materials.

units.passage: Uploading class/course material, lecture notes to any unauthorized G-AI tool (e.g., ChatGPT and others), or online learning platform (including Chegg, CourseHero, and other similar platforms)
units.why: "Uploading class/course material, lecture notes to any unauthorized G-AI tool" is not allowed: P49.

units.passage: Therefore, uploading any course content to any online portal, including online learning platforms such as Course Hero, Chegg, etc., or any Gen AI platforms (such as ChatGPT, CoPilot, Gemini, etc.) is illegal and strictly prohibited.
units.why: Uploading course content to GenAI platforms 'is illegal and strictly prohibited': P49.

units.passage: Simply stated: do not upload any course materials/content to any unauthorized site without the express written permission of the instructor/copyright holder
units.why: "do not upload any course materials/content to any unauthorized site without the express written permission of the instructor" says what permission is needed: P49.

units.passage: Do not upload course-specific materials—including assignment prompts, course code, datasets, class notes, hidden tests, solution keys, or other restricted content—to AI tools without the instructor’s explicit approval
units.why: 'Do not upload course-specific materials ... to AI tools without the instructor's explicit approval' protects course materials, P49.

units.passage: Faculty and students must follow Fair Use laws and policies with respect to use of copyrighted course materials or proprietary instructional resources in any AI tool.
units.why: 'Faculty and students must follow Fair Use laws and policies with respect to use of copyrighted course materials ... in any AI tool' limits putting course materials into AI, P49 with a fit note.
units.fit_note: Conditions use of copyrighted course materials in AI on Fair Use rather than banning uploads outright; copyright (P52) is also close. | Also touches uploading course materials to AI (P49) but permits fair-use compliance rather than banning. | Conditions use of copyrighted course materials in AI on Fair Use rather than banning uploads outright.

units.passage: Uploading confidential or copyrighted materials not permitted by course policy
units.why: 'Uploading confidential or copyrighted materials not permitted by course policy' is barred: P49.

units.passage: Tell your students whether you will allow them to upload your course materials into a generative AI tool.
units.why: The bullet "Tell your students whether you will allow them to upload your course materials into a generative AI tool" asks the instructor to state a position on uploading course materials, so it is a recommendation to the instructor under the guide's "we recommend" framing, not a ban itself (P49 with a fit note).
units.fit_note: A: Instructor must state a position; it does not itself forbid uploading. B: Instructor must state a rule on uploading materials; it does not itself ban it.

units.passage: It is a copyright violation to upload intellectual property / copyrighted materials (which includes student assignments, publisher materials, and articles obtained from the UCF library by download) to an AI tool that trains itself or stores such materials.
units.why: The passage says "It is a copyright violation to upload intellectual property / copyrighted materials" to a tool that trains on or stores them. It forbids an act done while using AI on work, so actor all, phase during-work, modality must-not, type P49 (do not upload course materials).
units.fit_note: Applies to tools that train on or store inputs and is framed as a copyright matter. | Framed as a copyright violation and limited to tools that train or store; also covers library downloads.

units.passage: Faculty intellectual property (IP), such as course materials and other instructional materials, may not be submitted to AI tools for model training or other secondary uses without their express permission.
units.why: "may not be submitted to AI tools for model training or other secondary uses without their express permission" protects faculty course materials from AI tools. P49 (do not upload course materials) is nearest; here the protected party is the faculty member and the concern is training.
units.fit_note: Binds all users, concerns model training and secondary uses, and allows the faculty member's express permission. / Concerns faculty IP and use for model training or secondary uses, with an exception by faculty permission; P49 is about students uploading materials.

units.passage: Original research or content that is owned by Cornell University, our students, or employees should not be uploaded to these tools, since they can become part of the training data used by the GAI tools.
units.why: The report says content 'owned by Cornell University, our students, or employees should not be uploaded to these tools', including student assignments and research data. The nearest type is P49 (do not upload course materials), but it also covers research data and PII, hence the fit note.
units.fit_note: Also covers research data, PII and partner data, not only course materials.

units.passage: Note that uploading documents to GenAI tools is a form of sharing.
units.why: The page quotes the Code: 'students may not share course material without instructor permission', and adds that uploading to GenAI is sharing. Do not upload course materials, so P49.
units.fit_note: Applies the Code's no-sharing rule to GenAI uploads.

units.passage: If you do not want your course material uploaded to GenAI, make that expectation clear to students in your syllabus and mention it explicitly in a class meeting.
units.why: Instructors who do not want material uploaded should say so in the syllabus and in class; communicating an upload rule: P49.
units.fit_note: Specifically about stating a no-upload expectation.

units.passage: This includes uploading work or submitting class assignments or exams to third party platforms and websites beyond those assigned for the class, such as commercial homework aggregators, without the proper authorization of a professor
units.policy: Uploading work or submitting class assignments or exams to third party platforms and websites beyond those assigned for the class is cheating without the professor's authorization.
units.why: Submitting class assignments or exams to third-party platforms beyond those assigned, without professor authorization, is cheating. It restricts uploading course work to outside tools, so P49.

units.passage: Students should not use University-approved AI tools to create, share, or distribute materials derived from course content without explicit permission from the instructor.
units.why: "Students should not use University-approved AI tools to create, share, or distribute materials derived from course content without explicit permission from the instructor" restricts uploading or reuse of course material, so P49; should-not.
units.fit_note: Covers creating and sharing materials derived from course content, with instructor permission as the exception.

units.passage: Do not share login credentials, course materials, research, or other information with AI tools that are not approved by the university.
units.policy: Do not share login credentials, course materials, research, or other information with AI tools that are not approved by the university.

units.why: 'You should not upload copyrighted materials into AI systems without proper authorization, including course materials'; P49 (do not upload course materials).

units.passage: And you should never submit the work of peers and instructors without their explicit consent
units.why: 'you should never submit the work of peers and instructors without their explicit consent' (to AI); P49 upload of others' material.

units.why: 'should not share recordings or AI-generated summaries with individuals outside the class without the instructor's consent'; P49.

units.why: 'GMU guidelines prohibit the uploading of another person's material to an AI tool or database without their permission.' P49.

units.passage: Before uploading something to a generative AI tool, do you have permission to do so?

units.passage: Be mindful of copyright and whether you have permission to use other people’s content (eg course materials or another student’s work).

units.passage: student work and other intellectual property should not be shared with third-party AI tools without student permission

units.passage: Scholastic dishonesty means plagiarism; cheating on assignments or examinations, including the unauthorized use of online learning support and testing platforms; engaging in unauthorized collaboration on academic work, including the posting of student-generated coursework on online learning support and testing platforms not approved for the specific course in question; taking, acquiring, or using course materials without faculty permission, including the posting of faculty-provided course materials on online learning and testing platforms; ...
units.why: Posting "faculty-provided course materials" on learning platforms is listed as scholastic dishonesty; since GenAI counts as such a platform, this bars uploading course materials to AI tools (P49).

units.passage: Indicate materials that may not be uploaded to GenAI tools.

units.passage: Do not upload application code or intellectual property (e.g., new inventions whether p atentable or unpatentable, human subjects research, copyrighted content, proprietary source code, etc.) into an AI system unless it is reviewed by the AI Review Committee and the Office of Information Security. 3.

units.policy: Instructors who are concerned about intellectual property may communicate to students that assignment prompts and other instructor-created materials are protected intellectual property, and that submitting those materials to an AI tool without permission might be a violation of intellectual property rights.
